name: Supervisor David Canepa
subject: 2024 May e-newsletter
body:
| | | |
---
| | |
# 2024 May e-newsletter
---
|
---
|
---
| **Beyond Differences offers curriculum for schools for youth suffering loneliness**
---
| Dear friends,

I was so honored to be invited as a guest speaker and to share the stage with Congresswoman-elect Lateefah Simon at the Beyond Differences fundraiser at Sweetwater in Mill Valley, Saturday, May 4.

I was particularly touched by the story of Lili, the daughter of Beyond Differences’ founders Laura Talmus and Ace Smith, who suffered social isolation for no reason other than she looked different. Lili was born with Apert Syndrome, a rare cranial-facial anomaly, which caused her peers and teachers to treat her differently than other students.

She was not bullied or teased but was often treated as if she were invisible. This behavior was just as insidious. Social isolation was not recognized as a serious public health issue at the time, which amplified Lili’s pain and loneliness.
---
Lili and her family believed that Apert Syndrome–or any difference for that matter – should never prevent young people from forming deep and meaningful relationships.

Sadly, in October 2009, Lili passed away unexpectedly in her sleep due to medical complications. She was only 151⁄2 years old.

Since San Mateo County was the first in the nation to declare loneliness a public health crisis, I have learned so much about the epidemic and its impacts on our youth, older adults and everyone in between.

I could tell how impactful Beyond Differences curriculum is as I listened to Avery, Briggs and Jacky (shown in the picture above) share the experiences they’ve had and the projects and presentations they’ve made to raise awareness of social isolation and loneliness. To learn more go to: [https://www.beyonddifferences.org/](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=d3762e330c&e=c0babbc643)
---
| **Bay Wheels bikeshare station debuts in San Mateo County**

May is National Bike month and I’m proud to announce that the Metropolitan Transportation Commission in partnership with Lyft has launched the first Bay Wheels bikeshare station in San Mateo County at the Daly City BART station.

This station paves the way for safer bicycling and its debut at Daly City BART, the ninth busiest in the system, can propel the Bay Area to be the most bike-friendly in the nation one day.

It’s a last-mile commute solution that is better for the environment and better for the mind and body. Today, Amsterdam is considered to be the most bike-friendly in the entire world but it was only a few decades ago that the city’s streets were clogged with cars like we are now. I’m proud to be a part of a growing movement that shows what a little pedal power can do.

The new docking station marks the first Bay Wheels location in San Mateo County and the continuation of a growth strategy that began last fall with the introduction of more than 1,500 new e-bikes and 30 new docking stations in San Francisco and San Jose and then shifted last month to the East Bay, where the system is adding 24 new docking stations and 565 next-generation e-bikes in Oakland, Emeryville and Berkeley.

Launched in 2017, Bay Wheels is the Bay Area’s regional bikeshare program with over 6,000 bicycles — both pedal-powered and pedal-assist electric bikes — at more than 500 stations in San Jose, San Francisco, Oakland, Berkeley, Emeryville and Daly City. Lyft operates Bay Wheels under a contract managed by MTC.

To learn more go to: [https://mtc.ca.gov/operations/traveler-services/bay-wheels-bike-share-program](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=85a4bd436b&e=c0babbc643)
---
---
| **Skyline Learning Communities celebrates $125,000 grant from my office**

It was nearly a year ago on May 23, 2023, that the Board of Supervisors approved my district discretionary Measure K request of $125,000 to benefit Skyline College’s Learning Communities, which honored me for the contribution Thursday, May 9.

Skyline’s learning communities such as UMOJA (African American), Puente (Latinx), Black and Brown Scholars, Women’s Leadership and Mentoring Academy (WMLA), Kababayan (Fliipinx), and First Year Experience (FYE) among others provide a supportive network of culturally competent faculty, staff, and administrators to help you reach your goals.

These are frankly programs that did not exist when I attended Skyline back in the early 90s.
It shows you how we are growing as a community to uplift all voices in this county, to provide an education and a pathway to a four-year-degree or a career in the trades.

The Measure K showcase held on campus is proof as I learn more about the learning community and affinity group projects that when government invests in culturally-competent education the results can be limitless.
---
| **New shuttle for Veterans Village in Colma prompted by outreach from 2 commissions**

May is Older Americans Month and I want to highlight and praise two county commissions, the Commission on Aging and the Veterans Commission, that prompted President Warren Slocum and I to fund startup costs of $26,000 for a new shuttle route that will serve the 70 residents who live at the Colma Veterans Village.

Last year, the two commissions came to us and recommended that the veterans who live at Colma Veterans Village needed better access to public transportation. The option available to these veterans, many with mobility issues, was the SamTrans bus service with bus stops in either direction over a half mile away.

At first, we were told that there was not a solution. We asked the transportation agency representatives to go back to the drawing table and find one for their veterans. And they did.

President Slocum and I met with officials from SamTrans, the City of South San Francisco and the Town of Colma over the ensuing months, and a solution for the veterans at Colma Veterans Village was found.

The City of South San Francisco already has free shuttle service in and around South San Francisco, which is funded through the City and a grant from SamTrans.

They agreed to expand shuttle service to and from Colma Veterans Village and the town of Colma agreed to assist with the funding, through June 2025 (when the next application to continue the South San Francisco Shuttle would occur).

After surveying the residents of Colma Veterans Village, a route has been established that will be free of charge and allow them to transfer to other routes within South San Francisco. The exciting news is that this route will begin operations at the end of May or in early June 2024.

This district-discretionary grant will enable South San Francisco, in collaboration with the town of Colma, to engage in outreach to expand free shuttle services to Colma Veterans Village, allowing the veteran residents ease of travel within Colma and South San Francisco. It will also allow for a special Memorial Day Shuttle to and from Colma Veterans Village to take the residents to the Memorial Day services at Golden Gate National Cemetery in San Bruno.

All said and done, this is great news for our veterans and we thank SamTrans and its CEO April Chan, the city of South San Francisco and its City Manager Sharon Ranals and the Town of Colma for this positive collaboration.

---
|
**May is Mental Health Month**

Each year, San Mateo County joins our state and country in celebrating Mental Health Month (MHM) in May. MHM is one of the best times of the year to increase awareness and inspire action to reduce stigma against those with mental health and substance use conditions. Each year the county partners with local agencies and community members to promote events free and open to the public throughout the county.

I am excited to share that the theme for 2024 May Mental Health Month is “Heal Through Connection #SMCAgainstLoneliness.”

The San Mateo County Board of Supervisors passed a resolution in January I sponsored declaring loneliness a public health crisis and pledging to promote social connection in our communities. According to the 2023 San Mateo County Health and Quality of Life Survey, 45% of residents in San Mateo County were experiencing difficulty with loneliness and isolation.

Now more than ever it is important that we find ways to connect with one another. This May, we encourage folks to connect with others at one of our free public events, connect to resources and connect with your community by getting involved.

I’d like to thank Mental Health Month Planning Committee co-Chairs Kristie Lui and Sylvia Tang for orchestrating a series of events this month to that brings our community together to engage in meaningful connectivity.

To learn more click here: [https://www.smchealth.org/mental-health-month](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=f794804447&e=c0babbc643)
---
| **Interns wanted to join our team ** We are looking to add to our great group of interns we are currently working with. If you or someone you know may be interested in applying to my Internship Program, submitting this form is the first step: [https://forms.gle/hiKqtn7Rird5vXwB9](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=2411f6b8c6&e=c0babbc643). You can also reach out to Mike Richardson on my staff directly with any questions at [mrichardson@smcgov.org](mailto:mrichardson@smcgov.org)
---
| **Battling food insecurity **
Food insecurity is a problem some residents may still face as we continue to emerge from the pandemic. Here are some resources residents can access: **CalFresh:**
Is a program for people with low-income who meet federal income eligibility rules and want to add to their budget to put healthy and nutritious food on the table. Website: [https://www.cdss.ca.gov/food-nutrition/calfresh](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=f3eb7abdbe&e=c0babbc643) Contact: (650) 802-6576, [antorres@smcgov.org](mailto:antorres@smcgov.org) **Daly City Partnership:**
DC Partnership is a local partnership that was formed to guide collaborative efforts and connect our community to services that promote well-being. Check out their website for times and locations. Website: [https://www.dcpartnership.org/covid19/](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=6e00a4e03e&e=c0babbc643) **Second Harvest Food Bank:**
Second Harvest offers food at various locations throughout San Mateo County listed on its webpage. Website: [https://www.shfb.org/get-food/](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=9853f5958c&e=c0babbc643) Contacts: Call (800) 984-3663 or text GETFOOD to (408) 455-5181 In friendship,
David J. Canepa
---

body:
I'll never stop fighting to protect voting rights, expand Vote by Mail, put an end to partisan gerrymandering, and get dark money out of our elections!
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/84892185/472966893/150430950?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTMyNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMmE3ZWI1NC03ODExLWVmMTEtOTZmMy02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=WzRM3kA4Q6AyF0MJSVXRjjJ4ZkzCV3uHyxolT_mF_UQ=&emci=d50f44c2-6611-ef11-96f3-6045bdd9e096&emdi=e2a7eb54-7811-ef11-96f3-6045bdd9e096&ceid=7731215)
---

| | We have a lot of work to do to defend our democracy against MAGA extremism. I know our grassroots team will never stop fighting to protect voting rights, expand Vote by Mail, put an end to partisan gerrymandering, and get dark money out of our elections! Across the country, we have five strong Democratic incumbents running in tough races this year who are also fighting to defend our democracy. **In Montana,** Senator Jon Tester is a longtime champion of transparency in our democracy. He helped pass sweeping ethics reform and then went above and beyond what was required and banned all gifts, meals, and travel from lobbyists for himself and his staff. He even barred any staffers who become lobbyists from lobbying him or being rehired. Jon's record on transparency earned him the title of "Montana's advocate for accountability." **In Ohio,** Senator Sherrod Brown is fighting voter suppression, particularly in his home state. Peter, today, I’m reflecting on some of my earliest days in politics.

In the middle of such a consequential election season, it can be easy to lose sight of our very modest beginnings. **But for me, remembering where I came from, and the difficulties we have faced along the way is so important to appreciating all those who made it possible, and how much people are depending on me.**

Before my run for the U.S. Senate or my tenure in the U.S. House of Representatives was even a thought, I served as California State Senator from 1996 to 2000. While going through family photos with Eve this weekend, we stumbled across this one:

No matter how big the challenge, this incredible team has helped us push forward. I haven’t walked any part of this path alone, and as Election Day gets closer, it’s a relief to know you’re by my side.

That said, Peter, I’m asking for your support again today. **We’re just 2 days away from our crucial mid-month fundraising deadline, and we’re falling behind.**

name: Katie Porter
subject: Money in politics is a huge and fundamental problem
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Truth to Power PAC
body:
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=38861%2E3422442%2E81yX5g)
Derek,
Money in politics is a huge and fundamental problem, and there are two main ways money influences elections.
1. Corporate PACs: Corporate PACs can give $5,000 to a candidate each election cycle. Now, individually that may not sound like a lot. But taken together, companies are able to team up and sway policy. For example, every Big Pharma company can give to a lawmaker, along with their trade group. Taken altogether, **it’s a system that results in legalized corruption and special privileges for corporate interests** —which stand in the way of higher wages, environmental protections, and even government oversight.
2. Super PACs: Super PACs can accept unlimited sums of money from just about anyone. In our own Senate race, super PACs spent more than $10M against us, and voters only learned which group was truly funding those ads after the election. **Super PACs, whether funded by conservative billionaires who are ideologically motivated, or by a corporate interest hoping to shore up a tax break or favorable regulations, threaten to undermine the fairness of our elections.** Each election cycle since the _Citizens United_ Supreme Court decision, they dump more and more money into races, eroding the faith Americans have in our political process.

Since getting to Congress in 2019, I’ve been leading the fight for campaign finance reform. But I’ll be honest, right now we don’t have the votes to pass the serious overhaul bill we need.
_**But right now, without passing a single bill, we can encourage Members of Congress to lead by example and reject corporate PAC money.**_ Every single Member has that choice, and while I’m proud that around 70 of my colleagues have joined me in rejecting it, that leaves over 460 people to go!
That’s where Truth to Power comes in: **I started this organization in 2020 to help elect Democrats who reject corporate PAC money**. By supporting these candidates—whether in competitive primaries or in purple districts, we can change this norm and create a Democratic party that isn’t beholden to corporate cash.
Truth to Power is grassroots funded, and so I can only continue this work with your support. **[Can you give a gift of $5 today that will power our fight?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ttp-em-20240513?refcode=em20240513-38861&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=38861_3422442_81yX5g&akid=38861%2E3422442%2E81yX5g)**

Many thanks for considering,
Katie

**Katie Porter started Truth to Power to support Democrats who reject corporate PAC money** and are running to protect the environment, restore the nationwide right to an abortion, and create an economy that works for working people. **[Donate ›››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/truth-to-power-1?refcode=em20240513-38861&amounts=&t=2&refcode2=38861_3422442_81yX5g&akid=38861%2E3422442%2E81yX5g)**

disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
#

Hey, it's Ruben Gallego. My friend, Senator Jon Tester, is running for re-election in Montana and needs our support. Please take a moment to read an important email from him below.

body:
#
We haven’t said much about our Democratic primary opponent since we first learned about him just a few weeks ago.
In that time, our challenger has self-financed 95% of his campaign to knock on doors all over New York’s 14th, calling Alexandria and our progressive movement ‘radical’ for wanting to tax the rich and guarantee healthcare for all.
**We’re fighting back with our _own_ grassroots canvassing:**
• While he blames our ‘extremist’ policies for skyrocketing inflation, we’ll focus on Alexandria’s work in Congress every day to hold corrupt interests and corporations accountable for price-gouging and exploitation.
• As he downplays his 25+ year career fighting for record profits on Wall Street, we’ll share how Alexandria has brought home millions of dollars for the working families of her district — while raising hundreds of thousands of dollars _just this year_ for abortion activists, healthcare organizers, and climate disaster recovery efforts, thanks to this grassroots movement.
• And although our opponent calls our movement a ‘left-wing political establishment,' we’ll keep having real conversations about how important Alexandria’s fight for measures like raising the minimum wage, universal health care, universal child care, and free college can be for working people living in financial uncertainty.
[Alexandria isn’t a multimillionaire self-financing her own campaign, and she takes $0 from corporations or Wall Street. | | China and the United States are set to sit down and discuss [defining](http://links.rogersforsenate.com/u/click?_t=b90de78796ce4ce596523293a2b8ff82&_m=8ed5fdc64be44c22ae341a9ebe427cb0&_e=Wc5wCjFBvTvox7dDjw034twZVXZQ-ZPyWsUHtruKTAP6HkflCkf17Ld5WenuKmEeg8nssEthO6d9l8iPrpYYdjfIvjgwHWRwvHjG2ynMMimBvwYowKsMnHXSrGvCbvSIvXKCuiVLHCXXzE9VRy3JtTTt7OhZb60GvXtG_0Zf_oJIYBnanPon_g1JM1cwFle56M2mJye-EiyBinuYNNs4BtCLoBWG51gqaPzYEMYEbcHVQ7sDESn43wWXw0hGMyPc) safety standards for artificial intelligence in Geneva this week. This sounds like a great idea and, if we had a reliable partner, it would be one. Setting up frameworks for the responsible development and use of what is likely to be one of the most profound technological innovations of this young century is vital to ensuring stability and security. The trouble is, we don’t have a reliable partner in China that we can trust. We have a strategic competitor that wants to not only win, but undermine our very way of life and democratic system. Talking is good, for sure, but our diplomats in Geneva have to know that what the Chinese Communist Party agrees to isn’t worth the paper it is printed on.

This is pretty important. I’m a former teacher, a Tennessee state legislator, and a proud member of the Tennessee Three. I’m running for U.S. Senate in Tennessee against one of the most extreme Republican senators in the country, Marsha Blackburn. You may recognize her as the bought-and-paid-for, anti-freedom politician who supports the most radical policies you can imagine. I am talking about nationwide-abortion-ban-level radical. It's time to put an end to her extremist politics. But to do that, I need your help. We’re coming up fast on our mid-May fundraising deadline. And with less than six months left until Election Day, we can’t afford to fall short of our $40,000 online goal. I know we can win this and defeat Marsha, but we don’t stand a fighting chance without our grassroots supporters. **_[Can I count on you to chip in $25 before the deadline on Wednesday to help us make a strong impact this month? >>>](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/84894975/472975478/209297649?amount=25&refcode=ea.a8593ea0-8411-ef11-96f3-6045bdd9e096&ms=ea.a8593ea0-8411-ef11-96f3-6045bdd9e096&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDYxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhODU5M2VhMC04NDExLWVmMTEtOTZmMy02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=HFFSVG-4Xusnpu4PGvs74CjIudGdKdYubBnlcOuRpHU=)_** Look, we’re up against a politician who, for decades, put her far-right politics and special interest pals before Tennessee and our country.
